q: Univalent foundations (Voevodsky) provides a set-level foundation via setoids or types with decidable equality. A 'set' in HoTT is a type A with:
opts: IsSet(A): all identity proofs in A are equal — (p q: a = b) → p = q (h-proposition level 1)
A has at least one element
exp: Sets in HoTT (h-sets or 0-types): A is a set if for any a, b: A, the type a =_A b is a mere proposition (h-Prop) — any two proofs of a = b are equal. This means A has no non-trivial homotopy (no higher structure). Classical mathematics lives in sets; HoTT adds higher types above them.
